title: Spectra of Random Polynomial Matrices: the Petaloid Law
summary: We study the distribution of the zeros of $\det P_N(z)$ where $P_N(z)$ is a random monic polynomial matrix, i.e., $P_N(z)=z^dI-\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}A_{j,N}z^j$ for possibly coupled random matrices $A_{j,N}$, scaled to have entrywise variance $O(1/N)$. We provide general conditions under which this distribution almost-surely weakly converges as $N\to\infty$ to a deterministic measure, depending on just the variance and covariance of the entries of the $A_j$. This generalizes the circular, elliptic, and semicircle laws, which concern the special case of this question where $d=1$. Unlike those…
